A genuinely strong top line — net sales SEK 29.2m (~$2.90m), +130% YoY and +38% QoQ with cash opex up only 6% QoQ — but the near-breakeven EBITDA is flattered by SEK 5.8m (~$0.58m) of capitalised development and the net loss by a SEK 1.7m (~$0.17m) non-cash FX gain; underlying EBITDA was SEK −6.6m (~$−0.66m) and free cash flow SEK −11.9m (~$−1.18m), roughly 3x the year-ago burn. The quarter closed with SEK 0.36m (~$0.04m) of cash and SEK −27.8m (~$−2.76m) of equity, forcing SEK 45.2m (~$4.50m) of directed issues at SEK 0.65 (32% dilution, ~SEK 23m net cash) — and the CFO resigned three days after the report. Shares +18% on the day; the real test is whether Q4 delivers the positive operating cash flow the board has pointed to.

Analyst report · 9M 2026 · Confidence high

Danske Spil

A flat nine months that hides a Q3 downturn: 9M-26 BSI (GGR) +0.5% to DKK 3,841m (~$568m) and net profit +1.5% to DKK 1,547m (~$229m) were carried entirely by H1; derived Q3 BSI fell 1.4% to DKK 1,255m (~$186m) and net profit fell 4.2% to DKK 503m (~$74m) as the lottery jackpot cycle turned (Danske Lotteri Spil -5.9%) and only cost cuts and a +7.5% licensed-games segment held EBIT margin flat at 52.7%. FY26 guidance (BSI DKK 5,200–5,300m / net profit DKK 1,950–2,050m) is unchanged and, with an October Eurojackpot max-pool run, remains achievable in the upper half — but the equity story is a monopoly lottery cash-cow with a shrinking retail footprint and a sub-scale, duty-heavy online business that is not out-growing its market.

Aristocrat Leisure Limited

A clean, Gaming-led FY26 (year to 30 Sep 2026): normalised NPATA A$1,578.5m (~US$1,080m) +1.8% reported / +9.7% constant currency and EPSA 259.3c (~US$1.77) +13% cc, built on ~6,500 net North American Gaming Operations adds to 81,678 units at a 39% share and A$1.93bn (~US$1.32bn) returned to shareholders. The quality fades into the second half — H2 NPATA A$784.5m (~US$537m) was -4% YoY reported (≈+4% cc, our estimate, vs +16% cc in H1), ~A$45m of Light & Wonder settlement recovery sits inside the "normalised" corporate line, Interactive margins fell 280bps and D&D ran ahead of guidance. The ~7% intraday sell-off (close -1.3% at A$65.02 / ~US$44.48) was about CEO Trevor Croker's April-2027 retirement and the unquantified "NPATA growth in cc" FY27 outlook, not the numbers.
